newsitem.title: JAPAN: ABOUT 10 NATIONS TO ATTEND IMF, THAI MEETING - SOURCE.
newsitem.headline: ABOUT 10 NATIONS TO ATTEND IMF, THAI MEETING - SOURCE.

text.p: About 10 countries, mainly from Asia, are likely attend a meeting in Tokyo on Monday hosted by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to help Thailand cope with its economic woes, an financial industry source said on Friday.
The countries will likely include Hong Kong, China, Singapore, Malaysia, Australia, the source said.
Another financial source said the meeting will also be attended by the United States.
The meeting, expected to start from around 10 a.m. (0100 GMT) at the Imperial Hotel in Tokyo, will discuss details of an economic rescue package for Thailand's ailing economy.
The first source said he did not expect any concrete agreement on the amount of money Thailand will get from the IMF and other countries to address its economic woes during the meeting.

Rather, the meeting will be mainly for Thailand and the IMF to explain to potential donor nations what steps Thailand will implement to improve its economy and what would be needed to help the country, he said.
Asked whether the countries participating in the scheme will be limited to the 10 countries that will be attending the meeting, the source said he did not know.
An international monetary source said the IMF will be represented by Deputy Managing Director Shigemitsu Sugisaki, in place of IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus.
